entries.title: Monitor "No signal": wrong input source
entries.spot_it: The monitor shows a "No signal" or "Input" banner, and the cable is visibly in a port like DP while the monitor input is HDMI.
entries.correct_method: Press the monitor's input or source button and choose the port the cable is actually in. Check the port label on the back.

entries.title: HDMI/DP not fully seated
entries.spot_it: A metal part of the plug is visible outside the socket, or the plug is angled.
entries.correct_method: Push straight in until it stops. A DisplayPort plug should click. Check both ends.

entries.title: Desktop video cable in the motherboard instead of the graphics card
entries.spot_it: The video cable is in a port near the USB/audio cluster while a separate graphics card has its own ports lower down.
entries.correct_method: Move the cable to the ports on the graphics card (the horizontal strip lower on the back).

entries.title: USB-C cable is charge-only
entries.spot_it: The device charges but there's no display or data. The cable is thin or came with a phone charger.
entries.correct_method: Use a cable rated for data or video (USB 3.x/Thunderbolt logo, or the one that came with the monitor or dock).

entries.title: Modem cable in a router LAN port instead of WAN
entries.spot_it: The cable from the modem or wall goes into one of a group of same-colored ports. The WAN/Internet port is usually a different color or set apart.
entries.correct_method: Move it to the port labelled WAN or Internet, then restart the router.

entries.title: No link lights on the Ethernet port
entries.spot_it: The LEDs next to the port are off even though a cable is plugged in.
entries.correct_method: Reseat both ends until they click, try another port or cable, and check that the other device is powered on.

entries.title: RAM not fully latched
entries.spot_it: One end of the stick sits higher, or a clip isn't closed.
entries.correct_method: Line up the notch, then press firmly on both ends until both clips snap shut. Power is off.

entries.title: CPU 8-pin (EPS) power missing
entries.spot_it: An empty 4+4 or 8-pin socket in the top-left corner of the motherboard.
entries.correct_method: Connect the PSU cable labelled CPU (not PCIe) until it latches.

entries.title: Front-panel power switch on the wrong pins
entries.spot_it: Tiny two-pin connectors on the bottom-right header don't match the printed labels.
entries.correct_method: Check the motherboard manual's front-panel diagram (lookup_manual). PWR_SW goes on the PWR pins, and polarity doesn't matter for switches.
